text: Nothing in this Chapter prohibits: (a) an applicant from drafting their own specification or appearing/acting before the Controller; or (b) an advocate (not a patent agent) from taking part in a hearing before the Controller on behalf of a party.
plain_english_summary: Preserves a self-represented applicant's right to act pro se, and an advocate's right to appear at Controller hearings, without needing separate patent-agent registration.

title: Convention countries
text: Any country (or group/union of countries, or intergovernmental organisation) that is a party to an international/regional/bilateral treaty to which India is also a party, and which affords Indian applicants/citizens privileges similar to those given its own citizens for patent grant/protection, is a 'convention country' under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Defines the reciprocity basis for 'convention country' status, which underlies convention-priority filings under sections 135-139 (India's equivalent of Paris Convention priority claims).

title: Notification as to countries not providing for reciprocity
text: Where a notified country does not accord Indian citizens the same patent rights it accords its own nationals, that country's nationals cannot apply for, or be registered as proprietor/assignee of, an Indian patent, or hold/apply for a licence under one.
plain_english_summary: A reciprocity-enforcement tool — the Central Government can bar nationals of non-reciprocating countries from applying for, holding, or licensing Indian patents.

title: Convention applications
text: (1) Where a person files a 'basic application' in a convention country and files the corresponding Indian application within twelve months, the priority date of claims based on the basic application's disclosure is the basic application's filing date.

sub_structure.explanation: Explanation: where similar protection was sought in multiple convention countries, the twelve months runs from the earliest such application.
sub_structure.2: (2) A single convention application may cover cognate/related inventions from multiple convention-country applications, filed within twelve months of the earliest.

plain_english_summary: The core convention-priority mechanism — files an Indian application within 12 months of a first foreign filing (e.g. a US provisional) and claims that earlier priority date, the standard Paris Convention route most software startups use for their first Indian filing after filing abroad.

title: Special provisions relating to convention application
text: (1) Every convention application must be accompanied by a complete specification, specify the date/country of the first foreign application, and state no earlier convention-country application was made for the invention.

sub_structure.3: (3) A convention application cannot be post-dated under section 17(1) beyond the date on which it could otherwise have been made.

plain_english_summary: Sets the specific formal content and dating requirements for convention (Paris Convention priority) applications filed in India.

title: Multiple priorities
text: (1) Where related inventions were the subject of multiple convention-country applications constituting one invention, a single application may be filed within twelve months of the earliest, covering the inventions in the basic applications' specifications.

sub_structure.2: (2) The priority date of a claim based on matter in one or more basic applications is the date that matter was first disclosed.

plain_english_summary: Allows combining multiple related foreign priority filings into one Indian application, with each claim taking the priority date of whichever basic application first disclosed its subject matter.

title: Supplementary provisions as to convention applications
text: (1)-(2) On request, the applicant must furnish verified copies (and English translations, if foreign-language) of the corresponding foreign specification/documents.

sub_structure.4: (4) A PCT international application designating India has effect as a filing under sections 7, 54 and 135, with its title/description/claims/abstract/drawings treated as the complete specification.
sub_structure.5: (5) The filing date for such applications is the international filing date under the PCT.

plain_english_summary: Supplements the convention-application regime, and critically confirms that PCT national-phase entries into India are treated exactly like domestic applications with the international filing date preserved — the operative rule for PCT-based Indian patent strategy.

title: Other provisions of Act to apply to convention applications
text: Save as otherwise provided in this Chapter, all other provisions of the Act apply to a convention application and any patent granted on it, as they apply to an ordinary application/patent.
plain_english_summary: A general saving clause confirming convention applications are otherwise treated identically to ordinary Indian applications throughout prosecution, grant, and enforcement.

title: Avoidance of certain restrictive conditions
text: (1) It is unlawful to insert, in a contract for sale/lease of a patented article (or article made by a patented process), or in a licence to manufacture/use a patented article or to work a patented process, a condition that: (a) ties the purchaser/lessee/licensee to acquiring non-patented articles only from the vendor/lessor/licensor or their nominees (or restricts acquiring them elsewhere); (b) prohibits or restricts using a non-patented article not supplied by the vendor/lessor/licensor; (c) prohibits or restricts using a non-patented process other than the patented one; or (d) imposes exclusive grant-back, prevents challenges to the patent's validity, or amounts to coercive package licensing. Any such condition is void.

sub_structure.2: (2) Splitting such a condition into a separately-executed agreement does not exempt it from this section.
sub_structure.3: (3) In an infringement proceeding, it is a defence to prove an unlawful condition of this kind was in force under a contract relating to the patent — unless the plaintiff is not a party to that contract and proves the condition was inserted without their knowledge/consent.
sub_structure.4: (4) This section does not: (a) affect a condition prohibiting sale of goods other than a particular person's; (b) validate an otherwise-invalid contract; or (c) affect a lease/licence condition reserving to the lessor/licensor the right to supply replacement parts or repair the patented article.

plain_english_summary: India's anti-tying and anti-abusive-licensing-term provision for patents — directly parallel to section 42 of the Designs Act. Void per se are: exclusive-sourcing/tying clauses, restrictions on using competing non-patented products/processes, exclusive grant-back obligations, no-challenge (non-assertion of invalidity) clauses, and coercive package/bundled licensing. This is the single most important provision to check when drafting or reviewing a patent licence agreement for a software-related invention — common SaaS/technology licensing clauses like 'you may not challenge the validity of our patents' or 'you must license our entire patent bundle, not individual patents' risk being struck down as void under this section, with a defendant able to raise the illegal condition as a full defence to an infringement claim.

title: Determination of certain contracts
text: (1) Once all patents protecting a product/process covered by a sale/lease/manufacture/use/licence contract have ceased to be in force, the purchaser/lessee/licensee may terminate that contract (notwithstanding any contrary term) by giving three months' written notice.

sub_structure.2: (2) This is without prejudice to any other right to terminate the contract that exists independently of this section.

plain_english_summary: Gives a patent licensee/purchaser a statutory right to exit a patent-related contract once the underlying patent(s) expire — a mandatory 'sunset' termination right that overrides contrary contract terms (e.g. a fixed multi-year term that would otherwise survive patent expiry), relevant when structuring the term/termination clauses of a patent licence agreement.

title: Fees
text: (1) Prescribed fees are payable for the grant of patents, applications, and other prescribed matters relating to patent grant. (2) The Controller need not act until a payable fee is paid. (3) A document requiring a fee is deemed not filed if the fee isn't paid within the prescribed time.

sub_structure.4: (4) Where a principal patent is granted more than two years after filing, fees that fell due in the meantime may be paid within three months of the patent being recorded (extendable to nine months).

plain_english_summary: The general fee-payment framework underlying all Patent Office transactions, including a grace period for fees that accrue during a long pendency before grant.

title: Restrictions upon publication of specification
text: Subject to Chapter VII (secrecy), an application and any specification filed with it shall not, without the applicant's consent, be published before expiry of the section 11A(1) prescribed period, or before it becomes open for public inspection under section 11A(3) or section 43.
plain_english_summary: Confirms the confidentiality of applications/specifications before the statutory publication trigger points, subject to the applicant's own consent to earlier publication.

title: Reports of examiners to be confidential
text: Examiners' reports to the Controller are not open to public inspection or publication, and are not liable to production/inspection in legal proceedings unless the court certifies production/inspection is desirable in the interests of justice.
plain_english_summary: Keeps internal examiner reports confidential by default, shielding the Patent Office's internal deliberative process from routine discovery — a court order is needed to unseal them.

title: Publication of official journal
text: The Controller shall periodically publish an official journal containing information required to be published under the Act or rules.
plain_english_summary: The statutory basis for the Patent Office's official journal, through which applications, grants, oppositions and other statutory notices are published.

title: Power of Controller to call for information from patentees
text: (1) The Controller may, by written notice, require a patentee or licensee (exclusive or otherwise) to furnish, within two months (or longer, if allowed), information/statements on the extent to which the patented invention has been commercially worked in India.

sub_structure.2: (2) Every patentee and licensee must, independently, furnish prescribed 'working' statements at prescribed intervals (not less than six months).
sub_structure.3: (3) The Controller may publish information received under this section.

plain_english_summary: Requires every Indian patentee (and licensee) to periodically file statements on how far the patented invention is being commercially worked in India — the statutory 'Form 27' working-statement obligation, backed by penalties under section 122, and a key ongoing compliance duty for any startup that holds a granted Indian patent.

title: Evidence of entries, documents, etc.
text: (1) A Controller-signed certificate as to any authorised entry/matter/thing is prima facie evidence of it. (2) A certified copy of a register entry, document, or patent is admissible in evidence in all courts without further proof of the original.

sub_structure.3: (3) The Controller/patent office officers are not compellable, in proceedings to which they are not a party, to produce the register/documents or testify, absent special court order.

plain_english_summary: Simplifies proof of Patent Office records in litigation — certified copies are self-authenticating evidence, and Patent Office staff are generally shielded from being compelled to testify.

title: Declaration by infant, lunatic etc.
text: (1) Where a person is incapable (due to minority, lunacy, or other disability) of making a statement/doing an act required under this Act, their lawful guardian/committee/manager (or a court-appointed person) may act on their behalf.

sub_structure.2: (2) The court may appoint such a person on petition by anyone acting on the disabled person's behalf, or any other interested person.

plain_english_summary: Allows a guardian or court-appointed representative to act for an inventor/applicant who is a minor or under a legal disability.

title: Service of notices, etc., by post
text: Any notice, application or document required/authorised under this Act may be given, made or filed by post.
plain_english_summary: Confirms postal service is an acceptable method for Patent Act notices and filings.

title: Security for costs
text: Where a party giving notice of opposition, or applying for a compulsory licence, neither resides nor carries on business in India, the Controller may require security for costs, and may treat the opposition/application as abandoned if security is not given.
plain_english_summary: Protects Indian respondents from costs-recovery difficulties against foreign opponents/applicants by allowing the Controller to demand upfront security for costs.

title: Transmission of orders of courts to Controller
text: (1) Every High Court/Appellate Board order on a revocation petition (including validity certificates) must be sent to the Controller for entry in the register.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where a court's infringement/section 106 suit decides claim validity, the court must transmit its judgment/decree to the Controller for entry in a supplemental record.

plain_english_summary: Ensures court and Appellate Board decisions on patent validity/revocation are formally recorded in the official register, keeping it synchronized with litigation outcomes.

title: Information relating to patents
text: A person requesting prescribed information about a specified patent or patent application, in the prescribed manner and on payment of the prescribed fee, is entitled to have that information supplied.
plain_english_summary: Provides a formal statutory information-request channel to obtain prescribed details about a specific patent/application from the Patent Office.

title: Loss or destruction of patents
text: If a patent document is lost or destroyed (or its non-production is satisfactorily explained), the Controller may, on application and payment of the prescribed fee, issue a sealed duplicate.
plain_english_summary: Allows a patentee to obtain a replacement sealed patent document if the original is lost or destroyed.

title: Reports of Controller to be placed before Parliament
text: The Central Government shall cause an annual report on the execution of this Act by/under the Controller to be placed before both Houses of Parliament.
plain_english_summary: Requires annual parliamentary reporting on the Patent Office's administration of the Act — a transparency/accountability mechanism.

title: Patent to bind Government
text: Subject to the Act's other provisions, a patent has the like effect against the Government as it has against any person.
plain_english_summary: Confirms patents are generally enforceable against the Government itself, subject to the Chapter XVII carve-outs for authorised Government use/acquisition.

title: Right of Government to sell or use forfeited articles
text: Nothing in this Act affects the Government's (or its successors-in-title's) power to sell or use articles forfeited under any other law in force.
plain_english_summary: A narrow saving clause preserving the Government's power over separately-forfeited articles regardless of patent status.

title: Protection of security of India
text: Notwithstanding anything in this Act, the Central Government shall (a) not disclose information about a patentable invention/application it considers prejudicial to India's security, and (b) may take any action (including patent revocation) it considers necessary for India's security, by Gazette notification.

sub_structure.explanation: Explanation: 'security of India' includes matters relating to fissionable materials, arms/ammunition/war-materiel traffic, or actions taken in wartime or other international-relations emergencies.

plain_english_summary: A broad national-security override letting the Central Government withhold sensitive patent information or revoke a patent outright wherever it considers this necessary for India's security — a sweeping and largely unreviewable power added by the 2002 amendment, with obvious relevance to dual-use/defence-adjacent technology.

title: Power of High Courts to make rules
text: The High Court may make rules, consistent with this Act, as to the conduct and procedure of proceedings before it under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Delegated rule-making power letting each High Court set its own procedural rules for patent litigation before it.

title: Power of Central Government to make rules
text: (1) The Central Government may, by Gazette notification, make rules to carry out the Act's purposes.

sub_structure.2_selected: (2) Without prejudice to that generality, rules may cover matters such as: application/specification filing formats and timelines; fees and payment timing; examiner-report matters; procedure for disposing of pre-grant representations (s.25(1)) and s.39 applications; notice forms/timing; register maintenance (including electronic form); scientific-adviser qualifications (s.115); Appellate Board staff salaries/procedure and appeal forms/fees (ss.117, 117A, 117D); patent-agent register maintenance and qualifying examinations (s.125); and indexing/abridgement of specifications.
sub_structure.3: (3) Rule-making is subject to prior publication of draft rules, unless the Central Government dispenses with this where circumstances make it impracticable.

plain_english_summary: The Central Government's general delegated rule-making power (implemented via the Patents Rules, 2003) covering the detailed procedural machinery of the Act — fees, forms, timelines, and electronic recordkeeping — subject to a public-comment (prior-publication) requirement.

title: Rules to be placed before Parliament
text: Every rule made under this Act shall be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days (in one or more sessions); both Houses may modify or annul it within that window, without prejudice to anything already done under the rule.
plain_english_summary: The standard 30-day parliamentary 'laying' requirement for delegated rules under the Act, mirroring the equivalent provisions in the Designs and Trade Marks Acts.

title: Repeal of Act 2 of 1911 in so far as it relates to patents and savings
text: (1) The Indian Patents and Designs Act, 1911, so far as it relates to patents, is repealed, with the said 1911 Act amended as specified in the Schedule (relating to designs, which the 1911 Act continued to govern until the Designs Act, 2000).

sub_structure.4: (4) This section's specific mentions do not prejudice the General Clauses Act, 1897's general application to repeals.
sub_structure.5: (5) Pending infringement suits/revocation proceedings at the Act's commencement may continue and be disposed of as if this Act had not been passed.

plain_english_summary: The repeal-and-savings clause transitioning from the 1911 Act to this Act, preserving pending litigation and leaving the 1911 Act's design provisions (as amended by the Schedule) temporarily in force until superseded by the Designs Act, 2000.
